newsitem.title: GERMANY: Mercedes head sees solution in co. debate.
newsitem.headline: Mercedes head sees solution in co. debate.

text.p: Mercedes-Benz AG chairman Helmut Werner said he expected debate about the reorganisation of parent company Daimler-Benz AG will end in a "reasonable solution," a German newspaper said on Monday.
Werner told the daily Bild-Zeitung in an interview that he felt a responsibility to Daimler in planning for the reorganisation which is to be finalised on January 23.
"I am completely emotionally involved," Werner told the newspaper. A Mercedes spokesman confirmed that Werner had made the comments.

Werner and Daimler chairman Juergen Schrempp have been reported to be at odds about the future structure of Daimler. Schrempp aims to reduce the independence of individual units such as Mercedes, bringing them closer within the group struture.

The Mercedes chairman, whose unit is responsible for the bulk of Daimler's sales and profits, has opposed Schrempp's plans and has threatened to resign if Mercedes' independence is reduced, German newspaper and magazines have reported over the last few weeks.

Werner, who has been rumoured to be leaving Mercedes for positions at Volskwagen AG and German railway Deutsche Bahn, said he was concentrating on the Daimler restructuring and that the group should quickly arrive at a decision.
